title: Improving food security
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:43Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point covers cutting waste, soil care, trade and research, but the new point also needs fair trade rules, ending conflict and helping poorer farmers, which the card does not teach, and at Year 10 depth these additions are more than small changes.

draft.title: Improving food security
card: Food is lost or wasted all along the chain, from farm storage to shops to home bins. Cutting this waste means more of the food already grown reaches people, with no new land needed.
Sustainable yield growth means getting more food from the same land without damaging it. Examples are better seeds, drip irrigation and rotating crops to protect the soil.
Fair trade rules can stop rich countries blocking farm exports from poorer ones. Ending conflict matters too, because war can destroy farms, close markets and block food supplies.

Helping poorer farmers, for example with loans, training, storage and roads to markets, lifts their harvests and incomes. No single step is enough alone, but together they can feed more people without harming the environment.
draft.remember: Waste less, grow more with care, trade fairly, keep the peace and back small farmers.

opts: Rotating crops to protect the soil
Clearing forest to plant more crops
Using more water than the land can supply
Growing one crop each year until soil is worn out
a.why: Rotating crops gets more food from the same land and protects the soil. Clearing forest adds food by taking new land and harming the environment, so it is not sustainable yield growth.
a.clue: Look for more food from the same land, with no damage.

b.q: Many farmers in a poor region lose a lot of their harvest to rot before it reaches market. Which step would most directly cut this loss?
opts: Building cool storage and better roads to markets
Clearing more land to grow extra crops
Asking farmers to grow crops for biofuel
Waiting for the region's rainfall to increase
b.why: Storage and roads keep food from spoiling and help it reach buyers, which cuts waste and helps poorer farmers. Clearing more land adds food but does nothing about the loss, and it can harm the environment.
b.clue: The problem is food lost after harvest, not too little grown.

a.best: Rotating crops to protect the soil

b.best: Building cool storage and better roads to markets
